issues.issue_title: ETH driver regression in HAL_ETH_GetMACFilterConfig, HAL_ETH_SetMACFilterConfig
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: ETH driver regression in HAL_ETH_GetMACFilterConfig, HAL_ETH_SetMACFilterConfig
Context: repo=stm32f7xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=STM32F7XX, component=ETH, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=24
Root cause: Hello @pavel-a, Thank you for your report.
Fix: The meaning of bit 5 in MACFFR is "disable broadcast", so the bit set (1) means DISABLE.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: STM32F7XX, HAL, ETH, bug_report, high, bug, invalid, MACFFR, DISABLE

Technical details:
The meaning of bit 5 in MACFFR is "disable broadcast", so the bit set (1) means DISABLE. In these lines: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f7xx-hal-driver/blob/daf38ecc98298d8434a5fab8f5da35e34e4c1695/Src/stm32f7xx_hal_eth.c#L2461 https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f7xx-hal-driver/blob/daf38ecc98298d8434a5fab8f5da35e34e4c1695/Src/stm32f7xx_hal_eth.c#L2500 The change is part of commit 58f6d79 ; May 16, 2025 Please see also: https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus-embedded-software/enabling-igmp-disables-reception-of-broadcast-messages-v1-5-0/m-p/902322#M76083

Key comments:
Hello @pavel-a, Thank you for your report. The HAL_ETH_SetMACFilterConfig function configures the BroadcastFilter field, which maps to bit 5 (BFD, Broadcast Frames Disable) of the MACFFR register. When this bit is set to 1, broadcast packets are disabled. That is, setting BroadcastFilter = ENABLE enables the broadcast filter, which blocks broadcast frames. This matches the current implementation. [IMAGE ATTACHED] Thank you for clarification. If this is intended, please close.

issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Inconsistent DMA FIFO Error handling in STM32F7 SPI/PPP drivers compared to STM32H7
Context: repo=stm32f7xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=NUCLEO-F767ZI, component=DMA, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=23
Root cause: See also [stm32h7xx-hal-driver#76](https://github.
Fix: Hello ST, I would like to follow up on an issue that was originally reported by my colleague but for the STM32H7 family here: [STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver#76](https://github.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: NUCLEO-F767ZI, HAL, DMA, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, spi, STM32H7, GCC, HAL_DMA_Start_IT, FIFO

Technical details:
Hello ST, I would like to follow up on an issue that was originally reported by my colleague but for the STM32H7 family here: [STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver#76](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/issues/76). **Describe the set-up** - Nucleo-F767ZI - VS Code, GCC 13.3.1 (inside STM32CubeCLT 1.18.0), CMake, Ninja **Describe the bug** In stm32f7xx_hal_dma.c, the function HAL_DMA_Start_IT unconditionally enables the FIFO Error Interrupt (DMA_IT_FE), even when the DMA is used in Direct Mode (FIFO disabled). As discussed in the H7 issue mentioned above. In the STM32H7 HAL handles this in the PPP driver error callbacks. For example, in the H7 SPI driver: [stm32h7xx_hal_spi.c L3523](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/blob/57ed86b4c358e2333a71fd895b17f1ccdb68739e/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_spi.c#L3487) However STM32F7 HAL driver lacks this safeguard. In HAL_DMA_Start_IT, the DMA_IT_FE is unconditionally enabled and the SPI peripheral driver for F7 does not filter this error: [stm32f7xx_hal_spi.c L3375](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f7xx-hal-driver/blob/e1446fa12ffda80ea1016faf349e45b2047fff12/Src/stm32f7xx_hal_spi.c#L3375). This leads to triggered error callbacks for a feature that is not even active. **Questions:** 1. Could you please let us know if there are any plans to align the F7 drivers with the H7 implementation in the near release? 2. Just out of curiosity, why is this issue being addressed in PPP drivers instead of the DMA driver itself? I am not expert so definitely do not see whole context. Thank you for your time and have a nice day BR, Jan

Key comments:
See also [stm32h7xx-hal-driver#76](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/issues/76) Hello @JohnK1987, Thank you for highlighting this. I have shared your point with our team, especially regarding any plans to align the F7 drivers with the H7 implementation. I will keep you updated on any progress. Regarding the second point, the issue is being addressed within the PPP drivers rather than the DMA driver itself because: - The DMA driver is intentionally kept generic and “dumb”, it configures transfers and reports raw DMA status (transfer complete, error bits, etc.), but it does not know how these events should be interpreted for a specific peripheral or mode. That interpretation belongs to the PPP driver (SPI, UART, I2C, etc.), which is protocol‑aware and can decide whether a given DMA error is meaningful, ignorable, or critical in a given configuration. - Additionally, the same DMA controller is shared by many peripherals. If we change the behavior inside the DMA driver (for example, altering which interrupts are enabled or how some error bits are handled), we implicitly change it for all peripherals and all existing applications using DMA. issues.issue_title: Proposal: Prevent unused argument warning in HAL_EXTI_GetPending and HAL_EXTI_ClearPending
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Proposal: Prevent unused argument warning in HAL_EXTI_GetPending and HAL_EXTI_ClearPending
Context: repo=stm32f7xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=NUCLEO-F767ZI, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=22
Root cause: Hello @aschlueter-dev, Thank you for this heads-up.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** * Board: NUCLEO-F767ZI * IDE/Compiler: SEGGER Embedded Studio 8.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: NUCLEO-F767ZI, HAL, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, exti, IDE, SEGGER, HAL_EXTI_GetPending, HAL_EXTI_ClearPending, UNUSED

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * Board: NUCLEO-F767ZI * IDE/Compiler: SEGGER Embedded Studio 8.24 / SEGGER Compiler **Additional context** In the file stm32f7xx_hal_exti.c, I have added the following patch in the functions HAL_EXTI_GetPending and HAL_EXTI_ClearPending: c /* Prevent unused argument(s) compilation warning */ UNUSED(Edge); Details of the functions: c /** * @brief Get interrupt pending bit of a dedicated line. * @param hexti Exti handle. * @param Edge Specify which pending edge as to be checked. * This parameter can be one of the following values: * @arg @ref EXTI_TRIGGER_RISING_FALLING * This parameter is kept for compatibility with other series. * @retval 1 if interrupt is pending else 0. */ uint32_t HAL_EXTI_GetPending(EXTI_HandleTypeDef *hexti, uint32_t Edge) { uint32_t regval; uint32_t linepos; uint32_t maskline; /* Prevent unused argument(s) compilation warning */ UNUSED(Edge); /* Check parameters */ assert_param(IS_EXTI_LINE(hexti->Line)); assert_param(IS_EXTI_CONFIG_LINE(hexti->Line)); assert_param(IS_EXTI_PENDING_EDGE(Edge)); /* Compute line mask */ linepos = (hexti->Line & EXTI_PIN_MASK); maskline = (1uL << linepos); /* return 1 if bit is set else 0 */ regval = ((EXTI->PR & maskline) >> linepos); return regval; } /** * @brief Clear interrupt pending bit of a dedicated line. * @param hexti Exti handle. * @param Edge Specify which pending edge as to be clear. * This parameter can be one of the following values: * @arg @ref EXTI_TRIGGER_RISING_FALLING * This parameter is kept for compatibility with other series. * @retval None. */ void HAL_EXTI_ClearPending(EXTI_HandleTypeDef *hexti, uint32_t Edge) { uint32_t maskline; /* Prevent unused argument(s) compilation warning */ UNUSED(Edge); /* Check parameters */ assert_param(IS_EXTI_LINE(hexti->Line)); assert_param(IS_EXTI_CONFIG_LINE(hexti->Line)); assert_param(IS_EXTI_PENDING_EDGE(Edge)); /* Compute line mask */ maskline = (1uL << (hexti->Line & EXTI_PIN_MASK)); /* Clear Pending bit */ EXTI->PR = maskline; } **Question:** Is this fix in line with the project goals and would a pull request with this patch be welcome? Thank you!

Key comments:
Hello @aschlueter-dev, Thank you for this heads-up. Let's have this fixed. I'll log an internal tracker. ST Internal Reference: 219880 Fixed in Commit: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f7xx-hal-driver/commit/944feeabf699f73b3083167ff52a4ed77304def5

Problem: HAL_ETH broken after last update?
Context: repo=stm32f7xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=ETH, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=21
Root cause: Hello @micheledarold, Thank you for your report.
Fix: I use the latest version of hal_eth.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, ETH, bug_report, medium, bug, invalid, hal_eth, PTP, HAL_ETH_SetMACFilterConfig, HAL_ETH_GetMACFilterConfig, TCP, IMAGE

Technical details:
I use the latest version of hal_eth.c compared to previous version there are some modification on PTP related parts and other related to HAL_ETH_SetMACFilterConfig e HAL_ETH_GetMACFilterConfig these differences using the file with FreeRTOS+TCP v4.3.3 cause a problem in dhcp lease.. [IMAGE ATTACHED] according to RM0410 page 1825 when pFilterConfig->BroadcastFilter == ENABLE bit should be 1 not Bit 5 BFD: Broadcast frames disable When this bit is set, the address filters filter all incoming broadcast frames. When this bit is reset, the address filters pass all received broadcast frames. so I think that the new version is wrong on this part

Key comments:
Hello @micheledarold, Thank you for your report. When bit 5 of the configuration register is set to 1, broadcast packets are disabled, which means the Broadcast Filter is enabled. Conversely, when the Broadcast Filter is disabled, all broadcast packets should be allowed to pass through without restriction. This behavior is achieved by ensuring that bit 5 is cleared (set to 0) when the Broadcast Filter is disabled. ((uint32_t)((pFilterConfig->BroadcastFilter == ENABLE) ? 1U : 0U) << 5) this modification ensures that bit 5 is set to 1 when the Broadcast Filter is enabled, and cleared to 0 when it is disabled, thereby allowing all broadcast packets to pass when the filter is off. To port applications to the new HAL ETH driver, please configure the MAC filter as follows: - Set BroadcastFilter = DISABLE to allow reception of broadcast packets. - Set BroadcastFilter = ENABLE to block reception of broadcast packets. See also #20

Problem: LL ADC GetTriggerSource() returning zero
Context: repo=stm32f7xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=STM32F722ZE, component=ADC, layer=LL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=medium, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=17
Root cause: Hello @FelixBTR, First, thank you for your contribution, - The trigger source for regular ADC conversions is determined by the EXTSEL bits in the ADC_CR2 register.
Fix: **The set-up** * Custom board with STM32F722ZE processor * Visual Studio Code, with GNU ARM compiler gcc-arm-none-eabi-9-2019-q4-major * stm32f7xx-hal-driver version v1.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: STM32F722ZE, LL, ADC, usage_question, medium, question, hal, GNU, ARM, LL_ADC_REG_SetTriggerSource, ADC_TypeDef, LL_ADC_REG_GetTriggerSource

Technical details:
**The set-up** * Custom board with STM32F722ZE processor * Visual Studio Code, with GNU ARM compiler gcc-arm-none-eabi-9-2019-q4-major * stm32f7xx-hal-driver version v1.11.0 **Describe the bug** I am working on a system that modifies the trigger source of a regular group ADC conversion, in runtime. Using the LowLevel functions in stm32f7xx_ll_adc.h, I can set the trigger source by using: __STATIC_INLINE void LL_ADC_REG_SetTriggerSource(ADC_TypeDef *ADCx, uint32_t TriggerSource) I was hoping I could read back the value I set, but that is not the case. Using function: __STATIC_INLINE uint32_t LL_ADC_REG_GetTriggerSource(ADC_TypeDef *ADCx) This function returns zero for me. This is before actually starting conversions. **Additional context** I found that performing the & operation with ADC_REG_TRIG_SOURCE_MASK seems to delete the exact information I am interested in. See snippet below of this mask. /* Mask containing trigger source masks for each of possible */ /* trigger edge selection duplicated with shifts [0; 4; 8; 12] */ /* corresponding to {SW start; ext trigger; ext trigger; ext trigger}. */ #define ADC_REG_TRIG_SOURCE_MASK (((LL_ADC_REG_TRIG_SOFTWARE & ADC_CR2_EXTSEL) >> (4U * 0U)) | \ ((ADC_CR2_EXTSEL) >> (4U * 1U)) | \ ((ADC_CR2_EXTSEL) >> (4U * 2U)) | \ ((ADC_CR2_EXTSEL) >> (4U * 3U))) I don't really understand why there is a need for the extra logic in the Get version of the function. Looking at the Set version, it simply writes the TriggerSource value to the ADC_CR2_EXTSEL register bits of the ADC peripheral. Why does the Get care about ADC_CR2_EXTSEL, and apply shifts for that? Why does GetTriggerSource() not just get what SetTriggerSource() set? Am I doing something wrong, or is there indeed an issue with the current implementation? Do I need to have ADC_CR2_EXTEN (trigger edge detection) set at the time of using GetTriggerSource()? That would mean that GetTriggerSource() only gives valid return values after starting conversions using LL_ADC_REG_StartConversionExtTrig(). I would like to be able to r/w the trigger source, irrespective of whether or not conversions are happening. Is that possible? Thanks in advance.

Key comments:
Hello @FelixBTR, First, thank you for your contribution, - The trigger source for regular ADC conversions is determined by the EXTSEL bits in the ADC_CR2 register. - The trigger edge (rising/falling/both) is controlled by the EXTEN bits in the same register. The LL_ADC_REG_GetTriggerSource() function applies a mask (ADC_REG_TRIG_SOURCE_MASK) and possibly shifts, because the trigger source is only meaningful when the ADC is configured for an external trigger (when EXTEN is not zero). If EXTEN is zero (example: software trigger), the hardware ignores the EXTSEL bits, and the function may return zero or a default value. The mask and shifts in GetTriggerSource() are there to abstract the hardware behavior: - If the ADC is set for software trigger (EXTEN == 0), the function may return zero, as the trigger source is not relevant. - If the ADC is set for external trigger, the function extracts the correct bits for the trigger source. I hope this helps to answer your question. If you have any further questions or need additional assistance, please don’t hesitate to ask. Thank you! Technical details:
I'm trying to port a ptp library (ptp master) to a STM32F769 device on a stm32f769i-disco development board. Started with ethernetif.c from LwIP example, changed link_output function to call HAL_ETH_PTP_InsertTxTimestamp before HAL_ETH_Transmit_IT, this instructs ETH_DMA to perform time stamping. After packet being transmitted, HAL_ETH_PTP_GetTxTimestamp is called and the obtained timestamp is passed to ptp library which then use it for FollowUp message. Using wireshark I'm observing that the FollowUp messages contain timestamp from previous Sync message and not the last one. This looks like as if the tx descriptors index is off by one. I have confirmed that PTP is correctly configured with HAL_ETH_PTP_SetConfig and time set correctly. The question is what is the proper sequence to transmit and get timestamp or if is there any example with ptp from ST? I have figure it out, however HAL_ETH_PTP_GetTxTimestamp seams to have a bug, since it is returning time stamp from dmatxdesc->DESC0 and dmatxdesc->DESC1 intead of dmatxdesc->DESC6 and dmatxdesc->DESC7.

Hello @r315, Unfortunately, ST does not provide an official PTP example. However, the following resources may help you implement PTP on the STM32F769: [STM32F7 PTP Support](https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus-embedded-software/stm32f7-ptp-support/td-p/633500) [stm32_ptpd](https://github.com/mpthompson/stm32_ptpd) I'm already using those resources, and was able to implement a PTP master based on them. by porting ethernetif.c to use latest HAL_Driver. My understanding is that ST never had a example for PTP, not even for STM32MP1 family. Does it will ever be one? Hello @r315, Currently, we do not have an official example for PTP, and there is no plan to provide one in the near future. However, we appreciate your feedback and will take it into consideration for future development. Please allow me to close this issue. Thank you.

issues.issue_title: 8-Bit NOR devices cause hard fault on Hal_Nor_Init
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: 8-Bit NOR devices cause hard fault on Hal_Nor_Init
Context: repo=stm32f7xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=STM32F756BG, component=ETH, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=14
Root cause: My suggested fix; Or at least, something that works.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** * The board (either ST RPN reference or your custom board) * IDE or at least the compiler and its version Custom STM32F756BG Board.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: STM32F756BG, HAL, ETH, bug_report, high, bug, wontfix, internal bug tracker, fmc, nor, RPN, IDE

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * The board (either ST RPN reference or your custom board) * IDE or at least the compiler and its version Custom STM32F756BG Board. Macronix MX29LV040CTI (or any other 8-bit NOR flash) Visual Studio IDE; Code generated from STM32CubeMx. **Describe the bug** in HAL_NOR_Init, the code Hard Faults when setting the Nor ->CommandSet. Additionally, before this, the NOR_WRITE is writing 16-bit values to a 8-bit device. **How To Reproduce** 1- Spin up a project in stm32cubemx that has a NOR flash on NORSRAM_Bank_3 in Write mode (8-bit data) 2-Ensure the MPU is configured correctly 3- Generate Code 4- Run the code on a compatible board/device 2. The modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Driver, BSP, MW ...) HAL -> NOR 3. The use case that generates the problem When running HAL_NOR_Init in the FMC for a 8-bit parallel NOR flash chip **Additional context** ISSUE1: NOR_WRITE casts addresses to a 16-bit pointer. So when 'writing' to a 8-bit Flash, it is writing 2 bytes instead of just 1. ISSUE2: hnor->CommandSet = *(__IO uint16_t *) NOR_ADDR_SHIFT(deviceaddress, uwNORMemoryDataWidth, NOR_ADDRESS_COMMAND_SET); This line also has an explicit 16-bit cast. WHen working with 8-bit flash, this should be an 8-bit cast - THe 16-bit cast is causing a mis-aligned memory access when reading the command set (the address is 0x13... which is odd). Odd-alligned memory access is prohibited for 16-bit pointers. ISSUE3: ~this section~ C /* Get the value of the command set */ if (uwNORMemoryDataWidth == NOR_MEMORY_8B) { NOR_WRITE(NOR_ADDR_SHIFT(deviceaddress, uwNORMemoryDataWidth, NOR_CMD_ADDRESS_FIRST_CFI_BYTE), NOR_CMD_DATA_CFI); } else { NOR_WRITE(NOR_ADDR_SHIFT(deviceaddress, uwNORMemoryDataWidth, NOR_CMD_ADDRESS_FIRST_CFI), NOR_CMD_DATA_CFI); } ~is meaningless as written. the NOR_ADDR_SHIFT already takes the uwNORMemoryDataWidth into account. There does not need to be 2 separate calls for 2 addresses since the NOR_ADDR_SHIFT already modifies the address.~ This was a misunderstanding by me. The shift is indeed necessary. The issues raised here have implications for the rest of the HAL NOR. Anywhere that NOR_WRITE is used.

The easiest workaround, for now, is to declare the NOR flash as a 16-bit data width, and everything appears to work flawlessly (but i have not extensively tested this).... except every other byte is 0xFF! However, for the CFI Read, it requires writing 0x98 to _**0x55**_ instead of _**0xAA**_, as seen in my code snippet above. ~From my understanding, this is strange behavior.~ My datasheet is rather confusing. 0x55 is the expected address. 2. There are many spots in the HAL where NOR_WRITE calls must be cast to a __IO uint8_t * to prevent memory misallignment when trying to use the default __IO uint16_t *; these change must be made in the supplied HAL itself. 3. Problem: Cannot program internal flash with double word
Context: repo=stm32f7xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=NUCLEO-F767ZI, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=low, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=13
Root cause: Hello @satur9nine, Thank you for the report.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** * NUCLEO-F767ZI * ARM NONE EABI GCC 13.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: NUCLEO-F767ZI, HAL, usage_question, low, invalid, flash, ARM, NONE, EABI, GCC, PGP, HAL_StatusTypeDef

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * NUCLEO-F767ZI * ARM NONE EABI GCC 13.3 **Describe the bug** Flash program PGP error when trying to write double word to address 0x08010000 **How To Reproduce** Use the following code: HAL_StatusTypeDef status = HAL_OK; HAL_FLASH_Unlock(); uint64_t double_word_data 0xAA; status = HAL_FLASH_Program(FLASH_TYPEPROGRAM_DOUBLEWORD, 0x08010000, double_word_data); HAL_FLASH_Lock(); When using just single WORD programming it works. Datasheet DS11532 Rev 8 for "STM32F765xx STM32F767xx STM32F768Ax STM32F769xx" never mentions parallelism x64 anywhere. I think this chip doesn't really support double word programming. There are no examples of double word programming in STM32F7Cube. issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: STM32F723 does not trigger HAL_PCD_DataOutStageCallback for USB Audio on Windows
Context: repo=stm32f7xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=STM32F723, component=USB, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=8
Root cause: Hi @fxtentacle, Thank you for this report.
Fix: Dear STM team, When I created a new STM32F723ZETx project (FW v1.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: STM32F723, HAL, USB, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, STM, AUDIO_PeriodicTC_HS, STM32, DOEPCTL, EONUM

Technical details:
Dear STM team, When I created a new STM32F723ZETx project (FW v1.17.2) with STM32CubeMx and selected USB audio, then it worked nicely on Linux, but AUDIO_PeriodicTC_HS was never called on Windows. I've verified that Windows is sending isochronous audio packets, which means the problem is caused by the STM32 HAL not triggering the appropriate callbacks despite the hardware receiving the data. My impression is that this line: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f7xx_hal_driver/blob/52bfa97ba66afc08481f6fd7631322593bd89691/Src/stm32f7xx_hal_pcd.c#L1377 is trying to verify that the even/odd flag inside DOEPCTL is matching with the current frame number's parity. If that is the intention, then instead of ((RegVal & (0x1U << 16)) == (hpcd->FrameNumber & 0x1U))) it should read (((RegVal & (0x1U << 16)) != 0) == (hpcd->FrameNumber & 0x1U))) because we want to check if the EONUM bit is set and not check for its absolute value. And, indeed, that small change repairs the HAL_PCD_DataOutStageCallback on Windows :smiley:

Key comments:
Hi @fxtentacle, Thank you for this report. The point looks valid. A question though please. After you changed the code in the hal_pcd.c file, did you try again on Linux to check everything is still OK? Yes, the change had no influence on Linux where the HAL_PCD_DataOutStageCallback was being called both before and afterwards. My subjective impression is that Linux now has a slightly improved timing from when I connect the STM32 until when the audio device changes, but that's really hard to measure objectively. ST Internal Reference: 185291 Hi @fxtentacle, I hope you are doing well. Just to let you know that according to our development team, the fix should rather be as below, in order to check for both odd and even frames. c (((RegVal & (0x1U << 16)) >> 16) == (hpcd->FrameNumber & 0x1U))) Fixed in commit c393a68a4d63a50a4427d9f15ad128aa7dadab38
